title: Container build/test CI harness + base-image pinning policy (Docker + Apptainer)
context: All hands-on exercises and worked examples depend on reproducible, runnable containers. Without a CI harness, 'runnable' is asserted but not demonstrated; containers bit-rot silently and mislead learners. The harness builds each recipe from base images pinned by digest, runs smoke tests, and wires in the dataset-catalog validator, link/citation checker, and executable-example renderer so that a broken example fails the build. Bench scientists run on HPC, so Apptainer/Singularity definitions are required in addition to Docker. This task is a blocking prerequisite for all module authoring tasks (pilot-006 and all M1+ modules).
objective: Implement a CI harness that builds Docker and Apptainer/Singularity container recipes from pinned base images, runs smoke tests on a schedule, detects upstream drift marking lessons stale, and wires in the dataset-catalog validator, link/citation checker, and Quarto/papermill executable-example renderer as CI gates.
acceptanceCriteria: Builds each recipe from a base image pinned by digest (SHA256); pins package versions using a conda/mamba environment.yml with explicit versions or a lockfile.
Produces both a Dockerfile and an Apptainer/Singularity definition for every exercise/example recipe; both build successfully and pass a smoke test (container launches and a check script exits 0).
Scheduled CI rebuild (e.g., weekly) detects upstream base-image drift and marks affected lessons as stale, opening or commenting on a maintenance issue.

CI wires in: (1) dataset-catalog validator asserting every example references a PASS-gate entry, (2) link/citation checker asserting no dead links and flagged assertions carry citations, (3) executable-example renderer (Quarto render or papermill) verifying notebooks/documents produce output without error.
Repo tooling passes pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint; code licensed MIT; DCO signed off; no secrets, tokens, or credentials embedded in any container recipe or CI config.
CI configuration committed in the repo; reviewed and signed off by Technical reviewer.
resources: PLAN.md (Solution approach & architecture — CI / runnable means runnable)
template-004 (module template; exercises follow its structure)
output: A CI harness committed to the project repo as a PR: Dockerfile + Apptainer definition templates, a base-image pinning policy, a scheduled rebuild workflow (GitHub Actions or equivalent), and wired-in validators for dataset catalog, links/citations, and executable examples; pnpm build/test/lint green.
